Subject: Inference routing & cost vs hyperscalers — post-demo qualification

Sarah — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of call:
- AlphaMed wants predictable P95 latency under 120ms for short-form clinical prompts and predictable throughput for batch inference jobs.
- You're testing Redwood Dedicated vs running models on your hyperscaler fleet (mostly AWS G5 / G6 plans) to decide reservation vs cloud-on-demand path.
- Primary evaluation criteria: P95 latency, unit cost ($/1000 tokens or $/1k requests), warm/cold start behavior, and fallbacks during peak windows.

How Redwood differentiates (short):
- Dedicated capacity with guaranteed GPU pools + autoscale policies to meet throughput SLOs.
- Smart routing and prefix/KV caching to reduce per-token compute for repetitive clinical templates.
- Observability at token-level and rollback policies for safe fallbacks.

Suggested next tests (we think will be decisive):
1) Latency profile: p50/p95/p99 for 32-token and 256-token sequences (real prompt set — see attached sample).
2) Warm vs cold: repeated single-request latency after idle windows (5m, 30m, 4h).
3) Sustained throughput: 10-minute sustained run at target RPS (you mentioned target 250–500 rps) to validate queuing and concurrency.
4) Failure/fallback: simulated node-loss to validate routing to fallback model variant within the same region.

Logistics & asks:
- Can you confirm which hyperscaler SKUs you'd like us to compare against (AWS G5/G6, GCP A100 equivalents)?
- Are there any compliance checks (audit log granularity, retention) you need included in the PoC?

I've attached a short matrix that maps test cases to expected acceptance criteria and a PoC ops checklist. If those look right, we can schedule a 2-week dedicated trial with reserved capacity + engineered test harness.

Next step from our side: we can stand up the dedicated trial environment and a prebuilt test harness if you confirm scope today — aim to kick off next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Jonas
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

Sarah — answers below and a concrete next-step proposal. See attached matrix for exact thresholds and the PoC checklist.

Reserved commitments & guarantees (high level):
- Level-1 reserved: monthly GPU pool reserved (example: 4xA100-equivalent GPUs), 6- or 12-month term. Included: baseline throughput reservation and access to dedicated pool; we offer a 99.5% uptime SLA on the serving plane and a p95 latency SLO for pinned model families when you meet expected traffic shape.
- If you need contractual p95 guarantees for a specific latency number, we do custom SLAs tied to reservation size and network placement (region). That would be part of the dedicated contract.

Ballpark TCO for your baseline (100k requests/day, average 50 tokens per request):
- Hyperscaler (self-managed on G5/G6): approximate infra + ops: $5k–$8k/mo depending on bin-packing, autoscaling inefficiencies, and egress.
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved 4-GPU pool): estimated $3.5k–$5k/mo for the same token volume when using prefix/KV caching and continuous batching. Assumptions attached; we’ll run exact numbers once you share the sample load.

Key performance expectations (based on our internal runs):
- 32-token prompts: p95 ~70–90ms on dedicated pool (region and kernel tuning dependent).
- 256-token prompts: p95 ~200–260ms (batched runs will show better amortized cost).
- Cold-starts: cold vs warm delta typically 200–500ms depending on model size; we recommend pinned warm instances for your low-latency paths.

Proposed tests for the PoC (we’ll supply scripts & dashboard):
- Latency sweep (32/256 tokens) — p50/p95/p99 + histogram. Acceptance: p95 < 120ms for target prompt set.
- Sustained throughput: 10-minute run at 300 rps with 95% of requests served under SLO.
- Cache-effectiveness: run repeated templated prompts to show cost reduction from KV/prefix caching (measured tokens served vs returned).
- Failure injection: take 1 node out and validate routing/fallback under load.

Attachments: poC ops checklist (details on scripts), and a short cost matrix. I've dropped a HubSpot link below with deal notes; will update as we run tests.

If that aligns, proposed immediate step: confirm hyperscaler SKUs (you said AWS G5, G6, GCP A100) and we’ll schedule a 10–14 day reserved trial starting next Tue (2027-03-30). Please send the sample workload and any compliance thresholds for logs/audits.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
